rt.title: PLTS 100 GWp supply chain | Direktori METI
rt.deskripsi: Is local solar module supply enough for the 100 GWp solar programme? Capacity of 40 manufacturers, exports, local content, and factory locations, sourced and dated.
rt.judul: Solar module supply for the 100 GWp solar program
rt.kebutuhan: Programme demand and manufacturer capacity per year
rt.jawab: If the 100 GWp program is finished in {n} years, the need is about {butuh} GWp per year (EST). Module makers serving the local market have {lokal} GWp of capacity per year, about {persen}% of that need. Of the {total} GWp per year in total, {ekspor} GWp is export oriented.
rt.k.ekspor_cat: includes {gw} GWp from makers serving both local and export
rt.k.program_cat: The first {n} projects of the {target} GWp target, not yet installed
rt.b.label: Programme need versus manufacturer capacity, GWp per year
rt.horizon_cat: Target {target} GWp divided by {n} years. The source gives no completion date, so this is a scenario.
rt.peta_label: Interactive map of solar module factories; pan, zoom, or click a circle
rt.peta_cat: Dots are city centres from the source table (METI approximation), not factory coordinates.
rt.cara1: Need per year = programme target {target} GWp divided by the number of years. The source gives no completion date, so 5, 8, or 10 years is a scenario (Hypothesis), not an official target.
rt.cara2: Manufacturer capacity is the MWp per year column of the DJEBTKE ESDM table on solar module manufacturers, summed as given. Export-oriented = export market plus makers serving both (18.3 GWp), so pure local supply is a lower bound.
rt.cara3: Manufacturers that have not reported capacity (cells marked -) are not counted. Installed factory capacity is not actual output.
rt.cara4: TKDN: local content level, percent per the source table. BMP: company benefit weight, as given in the source table. APAMSI: Indonesian Solar Module Manufacturers Association.
rt.cara5: The share of demand met by local supply is calculated (EST): capacity of manufacturers serving the local market divided by yearly demand.
rt.kutip: Cite as: METI Directory, PLTS supply chain page, data frozen {tanggal}. Manufacturer source: DJEBTKE ESDM table on solar module manufacturers in Indonesia.

as.tren_label: Trend in {metrik}, last 10 years, 10 ASEAN countries with Indonesia highlighted
as.cara1: Renewable electricity share: percent of electricity generation from renewable sources (Ember, via Our World in Data, CC BY 4.0). Renewable capacity: IRENASTAT, total renewables in MW (Brunei not listed). Electricity access: World Bank WDI, percent of population.
as.cara2: Ranks are computed by METI from each country's latest-year value; the latest year can differ between countries (shown on each bar). Trends use the last 10 yearly points.
as.cara3: Changes in the trend table are calculated (EST): percentage-point difference for share and access, relative change for capacity. Share measures the generation mix, capacity measures installed power. They are not the same.
as.kutip: Cite as: METI Directory, ASEAN page, data frozen {tanggal}. Sources: Ember via Our World in Data, IRENASTAT, World Bank WDI.

ins.title: Indonesian renewable energy insights | Direktori METI
ins.deskripsi: Findings and trends computed directly from METI Directory data: projects, regulations, news, regions and the ASEAN comparison, with source, date and method.
ins.jawab: {n} cards computed from METI Directory data frozen on {tanggal}. Cards whose data is not available are not shown.
ins.s.proyek: METI Directory, tracked projects (RUPTL and public sources)
ins.s.berita: METI Directory, harvested news (GDELT and media feeds)
ins.s.kalender: METI Directory, calendar and activity log
ins.pip.j: Tracked projects target {mw} MW of additions from {a} to {b}, peaking in {puncak} at {mwp} MW.
ins.pip.vs: equal to {persen}% of the {mw} MW installed renewable capacity
ins.pip.chart: Added capacity by target COD year (MW)
ins.pip.cara: Projects that are not yet operating and have a capacity and a target COD are grouped by their earliest COD year, then the first capacity of each project is summed per year. The comparison is the sum of installed renewable capacity across 38 provinces (HEESI). This is an EST figure, not an official schedule: phased projects are counted in full in their earliest year.
ins.pip.penting: The more MW pile up in one year, the more likely schedules slip.
ins.tel.j: {n} projects ({mw} MW) passed their target COD before {tahun} but are not recorded as operating.
ins.tel.cara: Projects whose status is not operating and whose earliest COD year is before {tahun} count as late. A project in several programs is counted in each. Source status can lag the field, so this is an EST figure, not a verdict of delay.
ins.tel.penting: Delays usually come from funding, land, or permits. The cause should be checked with the developer.
ins.cel.j: {prov} has the largest geothermal gap. {gap} MW of potential is not yet installed, and only {persen}% is used.
ins.cel.chart: Geothermal potential, installed and remaining by province (MW)
ins.cel.cara: Remaining potential = a province's geothermal potential minus its installed geothermal capacity. Only geothermal is computed because per province solar, wind and hydro potential is not yet available as readable data (RUEN annex). EST figure.
ins.cel.penting: Provinces with a large gap matter most for the national geothermal target.
ins.plt.j: Local module makers supply only {persen}% of the yearly need for the 100 GWp solar program, which is {lokal} of {butuh} GWp.
ins.plt.chart: Yearly need and local solar module supply (GWp)
ins.plt.cara: Need per year = the {target} GWp target divided by 10 years (a Hypothesis scenario, no official schedule yet). Local supply = capacity of makers serving the domestic market, summed from the DJEBTKE ESDM table. Supply uses installed factory capacity, not actual output.
ins.plt.penting: The gap has to be covered by imports or new factories. This affects module prices and local content.
ins.mix.j: {tek} makes up {a}% of the project pipeline but only {b}% of installed capacity.
ins.mix.chart: Pipeline and installed capacity by technology (% of capacity)
ins.mix.cara: Pipeline = capacity of projects not yet operating, per technology. Installed = installed capacity per technology, summed over 38 provinces (HEESI). Both are limited to technologies present in both datasets, then turned into percentages of their totals. The card highlights the technology with the largest difference. EST figure.
ins.mix.penting: A large gap means the generation mix will shift and the grid needs to be ready.
ins.reg.j: {n} regulations were issued in the last 12 months, against {m} in the 12 months before. Of {total} recorded regulations, {dicabut} are revoked.
ins.reg.ruu: Latest activity on the EBET bill: {judul} ({tanggal}).
ins.reg.cara: Regulations are counted by enactment date in two 365-day windows ending on the data freeze date. Revoked counts come from the status in the data. The RUU EBET item comes from the METI calendar. Data coverage limits the numbers, so this is EST.
ins.reg.penting: Frequent rule changes make schedules and prices hard to plan. Check the status before relying on a regulation.
ins.ber.j: {tek} got the most coverage in the last 30 days, with {n} stories against {m} in the 30 days before.
ins.ber.cara: News items with a technology expertise label are counted per technology in two 30-day windows ending on the data freeze date. One item can carry several technology labels. Unlabeled items are left out. EST figure.
ins.ber.penting: News volume follows public and market attention.
ins.fin.j: State green sukuk allocated USD {usd} million to renewable energy (2018 to 2024, {persen}% of the total). The initial JETP commitment is USD {jetp} billion.
ins.fin.chart: Cumulative green sukuk allocation 2018 to 2024 (USD million)
ins.fin.cara: Figures are taken as published from the 2025 Green Sukuk Allocation and Impact Report (DJPPR Ministry of Finance): cumulative allocation to the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency sectors and to projects owned by the Ministry of Energy. ESDM-owned projects can overlap other sectors, so rows are not summed. The JETP commitment comes from the official JETP Indonesia site. Exchange rates and coupons are not recalculated.
ins.fin.penting: Planned projects need funding. A small renewable share means the allocated funds are still limited.
ins.asn.j: Indonesia ranks {r} of {n} ASEAN countries in renewable electricity share ({v}%), against an ASEAN median of {med}%.
ins.asn.chart: Renewable electricity share by ASEAN country (%)
ins.asn.cara: Renewable share of total electricity generation in each country's latest data year (Ember via Our World in Data). Rank is from the largest share; the median covers countries with data. Data years can differ between countries, so EST.
ins.asn.penting: Other ASEAN countries compete for clean energy investment.
ins.tk.j: Installed renewable capacity in Indonesia rose from {va} MW ({a}) to {vb} MW ({b}).
ins.tk.chart: Installed renewable capacity of Indonesia per year (MW)
ins.tk.cara: Yearly series of Indonesia's total renewable capacity from IRENASTAT. The large number above is the last year minus the first year (EST).
ins.tk.penting: Steady growth in capacity means real additions, not plans.
ins.tp.j: Project pipeline for technology {tek} in province {prov}. There are {n} projects by target COD year.
ins.tp.chart: Added capacity by target COD year (MW)
ins.tp.cara: Same as the pipeline card: projects not yet operating grouped by earliest COD year, then filtered by the technology and province above. Projects without a province drop out when a province is chosen. EST.
ins.tp.penting: Shows when added capacity is scheduled for one region or technology.
ins.tr.cara: Number of regulations by year enacted, and how many are now revoked by their year of issue. The year of revocation is not in the data, so the revoked line is not the count revoked each year. The latest year is incomplete. EST.
ins.tr.penting: Shows the years when many rules changed and how many no longer apply.
ins.tb.j: News per month for technology {tek}, {a} to {b}. There are {n} labelled stories.
ins.tb.cara: Technology-labeled news is counted by month of publication. With no technology chosen, the four technologies with the most items are shown. The news harvest only began in late July 2026, so the first and last months are incomplete. EST.
ins.tb.penting: Rises and falls in coverage show which technologies are being discussed.
ins.ta.j: Indonesia's renewable electricity share went from {va}% ({a}) to {vb}% ({b}); ASEAN median {med}%.
ins.ta.chart: Renewable electricity share, Indonesia and ASEAN median (%)
ins.ta.cara: Indonesia's yearly share from Ember via Our World in Data. The median is computed each year over ASEAN countries with data that year. The large number is the last year minus the first, in percentage points (EST).
ins.ta.penting: A flat share means renewables only keep pace with rising demand and have not replaced coal.
ins.cara1: All cards are calculated in the browser from Direktori METI data files when the page opens. The finding text is not hand-written. Only the explanatory sentence and the note on each card are.
ins.cara2: The EST label marks figures METI calculated from source data. The Hypothesis label marks figures that rest on an assumption, for example a 10-year schedule for the 100 GWp solar program.
ins.cara3: The Most important order is a METI team judgment of each finding's impact, not an automatic score. Cards whose data is not available, such as IDXCarbon carbon trading and green sukuk, stay hidden until the data arrives.
ins.cara4: Each card carries its source, data date and a denominator of the form n of N rows, so the share of data used is visible.
ins.kutip: Cite as: METI Directory, Insight page, data frozen {tanggal}. The source of each figure is on its card.

ins.kar.cara: Volume and value come from IDXCarbon monthly reports. Only months with a collected report are shown. A month missing from the chart is not yet recorded, which does not mean zero. The total adds up the months available. EST.
ins.kar.penting: Sharp swings in volume show a carbon market that is still thin.
ins.trf.j: Base tariffs for years 1 to 10 under Perpres 112/2022 range from {lo} ({tlo}) to {hi} ({thi}) US cents per kWh.
ins.trf.chart: Base tariff years 1 to 10 by technology, lowest to highest (US cents/kWh)
ins.trf.cara: Base values for years 1 to 10 from Annex I of Perpres 112/2022, grouped by technology; the bar shows the highest value and the text the range across capacity classes. The actual tariff is multiplied by factor F and a location multiplier, so this is a base bound, not a selling price. The table was OCR transcribed and can be changed by a ministerial decree; recheck before citing. EST.
ins.trf.penting: The base tariff decides whether a small project is viable. Differences between technologies show which are best protected by price.

ins.tkar.cara: Transaction value each month in million rupiah from the IDXCarbon monthly reports. Months without a report are left empty and the line connects the months that exist. EST.
ins.tkar.penting: A value that spikes in one month and falls back points to a large one-off transaction.
